parsed.summary: You lost a bag with your phone and bank card in a taxi in Tunisia. You need to block the card, secure the phone, and report the loss to the police (and optionally on Lqitha) to protect your accounts and obtain a replacement ID documents if needed.

steps.action: Call your bank’s emergency number (found on the back of the card or in the mobile app) and request an opposition/block on the card. If your banking app allows, block it directly from the app. Verify recent transactions for any unauthorized activity.

steps.when: Immediately after the card is blocked
steps.action: Contact your mobile operator (Tunisie Telecom, Ooredoo, or Orange) from another phone and ask them to suspend the SIM. Request a new SIM with the same number, providing your ID. If the phone is not locked, use Find My iPhone or Find My Device to locate or remotely lock/wipe it.

File a police report for the loss/ theft of the bag, phone and card. Call the police emergency line (197) or the national guard (193) and obtain an attestation of loss. Include details: taxi type, color, time, route, and any receipt or app reference.

Report the loss on the Lqitha platform, providing a detailed description of the bag, phone (brand, model, IMEI), and card. Attach the police attestation if possible. This increases the chance of recovery and creates an official record.

steps.when: After the card is blocked and police report filed
steps.action: Request a new bank card from your branch or via the app. Keep the opposition receipt for reference.

steps.when: If you need a new national ID or passport later
steps.action: Use the police attestation to request a duplicate CIN or passport within 30 days, as required by Loi organique n° 2024‑22.
